result.stdout:
Description:
  Indexes a markdown workspace and answers structural questions about it.

Usage:
  hippo [command] [options]

Options:
  -?, -h, --help  Show help and usage information
  --version       Show version information

Commands:
  init             Make the current folder a workspace by writing a starter .hippo/config.json
  index            Bring the index up to date with the workspace; every workspace command does this first, so index is only needed for --rebuild
  status           Show the workspace root, database path, file counts and last sweep
  find <query>     List indexed files in path order, or with a query, the pages holding every word and phrase of it, best match first, with a snippet of each
  show <path>      Show what the index holds for one file
  refs <path>      List the links out of a file, and whether each target exists
  backrefs <path>  List the links into a path
  lint             List broken links, frontmatter that fails to parse, and where OKF bundles depart from OKF v0.2; exits 1 when there are any findings
  cache            List the indexes in the cache, or remove those whose workspace is gone

Description:
  List indexed files in path order, or with a query, the pages holding every word and phrase of it, best match first, with a snippet of each

Usage:
  hippo find [<query>] [options]

Arguments:
  <query>  Words every page found must contain, and "phrases" each must contain as a whole; the shell needs a phrase quoted again, as '"two words"' (Windows PowerShell 5.1: '\"two words\"', cmd.exe: "\"two words\""); without a query, every indexed file is listed

Options:
  --glob <pattern>                Only paths matching this workspace-relative glob, or with a leading !, not matching it; repeatable
  --kind <markdown|other>         Only files of this kind
  --where <condition>             Only markdown files whose frontmatter field meets the condition: field=value, field!=value, field<value, field<=value, field>value, field>=value, field (present) or !field (missing); repeatable, and every condition must hold. A field is a dotted path, and a part ending in [] means each element of that list, as sources[].id=x. A value starting with @ names a field of the same page, as 'verified.at<@generated.at', and @@ writes a literal @; a value without a leading @ is always a literal. Numbers compare as numbers, anything else as text, so write dates as ISO 8601. Quote it for the shell, as --where 'as_of<2026-04-01'
  --field <path>                  Show this frontmatter field of each file, a dotted path such as verified.at, or several separated by commas; repeatable. A part ending in [] means each element of that list, so sources[].resource shows the list of values. A list or mapping shows whole; keys holding ., ,, [ or ] cannot be reached
  --errors                        Only files whose frontmatter failed to parse, with the error
  --no-refs                       Only files with no link to another indexed file
  --no-backrefs                   Only files no other file links to
  --from <pattern>                With --no-backrefs, count only links from files matching this workspace-relative glob, or with a leading !,

result.stdout:
Description:
  List the links into a path

Usage:
  hippo backrefs <path> [options]

Arguments:
  <path>  A path in the workspace, relative to the working directory: a file, a folder, or the workspace root; it need not exist, so links broken on it show; a folder's backrefs are the links to the folder itself, not to the files in it

Options:
  --link-kind <body|frontmatter>  Only links of this kind
  --from <pattern>                Only links from files matching this workspace-relative glob, or with a leading !, not matching it; repeatable
  --transitive                    Every file that reaches the path through a chain of links; --from and --link-kind apply at every hop
  --json                          Print JSON instead of text
  -?, -h, --help                  Show help and usage information

result.stdout:
Description:
  List broken links, frontmatter that fails to parse, and where OKF bundles depart from OKF v0.2; exits 1 when there are any findings

Usage:
  hippo lint [options]

Options:
  --rule <name>   Only this rule, even one lint.off turns off; * matches any run of characters, as in okf-*; repeatable
  --json          Print JSON instead of text
  -?, -h, --help  Show help and usage information

Rules:
  okf-type               A concept with no frontmatter, frontmatter that fails to parse, or no non-empty type
  okf-index-frontmatter  Frontmatter in an index.md below the bundle root, or a key other than okf_version in the root one
  okf-log-date           A level-2 heading in a log.md that is not a YYYY-MM-DD date
  okf-source-resource    A sources entry with no resource
  okf-footnote           A footnote whose label matches no sources[].id on its page
  okf-timestamp          A generated.at, verified[].at, stale_after, sources[].last_modified or usage_window that is not an ISO 8601 datetime with a UTC offset
  okf-actor              A generated with no by, or a generated.by or verified[].by not shaped <producer>/<version>, human:<id> or process:<id>
  okf-status             A status other than draft, stable or deprecated
  okf-index              An index.md entry whose page is missing or whose description is not the page's, or a page no index.md above it links to
  okf-version            A bundle whose okf_version is not 0.2, which hippo reads as 0.2 all the same
  broken-link            A path link whose target is neither an indexed file nor a folder holding one, or that leaves the workspace
  frontmatter-syntax     A markdown file whose frontmatter fails to parse
